recompute.summary: Confirmed. My independent plain-Python implementation of P, P2, G, K70, K50, GP and K70P, written from the protocol text and frozen before I read growth.py's code for them, reproduces the saved 30 paths to 0.000000 EUR at all six scenarios (balances, money paid in, stop-rule week), and reproduces a fresh run of all 2,000 paths cell for cell (5,772,000 balances and as many amounts paid, controls A, B, C, D, C2, D2 included). The single gap of my frozen version is a convention of the old shared code (the stake unit in a week that receives a payment), an ambiguity where growth.py's reading is at least as natural; it moves headline figures by 1 to 3 % and changes no conclusion. growth.summarise on a fresh run equals growth.json exactly; the old plans are unchanged (10,962 figures identical to the file saved before the change); gains are measured against the money really paid in, path by path. The 38 synthetic edge-case checks on growth.py's own engine pass (unconditional first three payments, test on the booked balance at the instant of the payment, skipped months never paid in P and caught up 1,000 at a time in P2, G bases switching strictly beyond -10 % and -20 %, bonus = 10 % of the gain in money, caps read on max(balance, paid)). The K floors were never crossed in 36,000 runs (worst -29.93 %, -49.93 %, -29.99 % of the money paid in). P at edge x-0.5: median paid in 3,000, median loss -2,886, no path loses more than it paid in; the 31.2 % of paths losing more than 3,000 all paid in more after their balance climbed back. What needs care is the framing, not the numbers: K70P and GP get their small losses by parking the robot after a bad start, which happens in about 1 path in 5 even with the full 2022-2025 edge (K70P x1: 21.8 % in loss at 36 months, 12.0 % stuck at 3,000 paid where C2 earned a median +104,812 on the same paths); P limits the amount exposed, not the rate of loss (median 94 % of the money put in is lost at x-0.5); K70 / K50 lose 30 % / 50 % of everything paid in (-10,508 / -17,343 at 36 months at x-0.5); no plan raises the early gain (12-month median at x1: C2 17,406 against 16,730 down to 5,949). In growth.json the fields paid / below_paid_pct / below_half_paid_pct of the plans with steps are against the nominal payments and should not be shown for them.

findings.what: Where the protection comes from: entirely from paying less money in the bad case, not from paying at the right time. The switch is a slow, sticky detector: reliable to say 'bad' after 6 to 12 months, unreliable to say 'good'. Inside a given scenario its timing has no value in this simulation (the draws make the future independent of the past) and it costs at half edge.

findings.what: Practicalities the user must be told. (a) The trial budget is risked at 5 % and is almost entirely lost when the rules are worthless; after that the account is too small to trade, which is how the loss stops. (b) A trial at 1 % loses less than half as much in the first year for the same information, but about the same after three years, with a slightly wider tail. (c) The rule is an instruction to the user and is made on the balance of closed trades.

findings.fix: Tell the user: 'You pay by hand, so each month the robot or a message must say pay or do not pay, comparing the balance of closed trades with the total you have paid in; open trades are ignored. The first 3,000 EUR are a trial budget risked at 5 % per trade: if the rules are worthless they are almost all lost, and the robot then can hardly place a trade. Run at 1 %, the same trial loses about 1,000 EUR in the first year instead of 2,500, at the cost of a lower gain when the robot is good (about 22,000 instead of 29,000 at half edge).' The 1 % variant is a diagnostic, not a declared plan.

findings.what: What a specialist would add, in plain words: why the steps limit the loss and why they cannot raise the average gain.
findings.evidence: Means at 36 months on the same 2,000 paths: edge 0: A +378, C2 -207, P -380, trial-only -474 (all about zero); edge 0.5: C2 54,003, P 42,161, A 39,461, blind calendar 43,599; edge 1: C2 197,499, P 186,940; edge -0.5: C2 -17,637, A -15,346, P -3,650. Shape at edge 0: A 56.3 % in loss with p10 -14,892; P 81.1 % in loss with p10 -6,751 and the same mean.
findings.fix: Wording: 'With the steps, new money goes in only when the robot has lost nothing so far: it is adding to a winner, at the level of the account. It limits the loss because a robot that loses falls under water early and then only the trial budget is exposed. It cannot raise the average gain: the next trade does not know whether the account is in profit, so the average result is the edge times the money exposed; less money exposed means a lower average when the edge is positive, zero when it is zero, and a smaller average loss when it is negative. What changes is the shape: many small losses and a few large gains, like an insurance paid for by more losing paths. The information on the rules is in the results counted in stakes, which do not depend on the size: a trial at 1 %, at the minimum lot or on the demo account tells the same thing for less money.'

critique.summary:
Verdict: confirmed with corrections. The main claim survives: among the declared plans, P is the one that cuts the loss most when the rules are worthless while keeping most of the gain at half edge. One sentence is false and five things are missing.

**The false sentence.** Pure floors do not "protect more but kill the gain". K70 loses about 10,500 EUR when the rules are worthless and gains about 31,000 at half edge; K50 about 17,300 and 40,000. P loses 2,900 and gains 29,000. Only GP and K70P cut the loss below 1,000 EUR, and only they kill the gain. The floors' real advantage is a loss capped by construction (K70 never worse than -10,800), which P does not have.

**What is missing.**
- **P is not a ceiling.** At edge -0.5 one path in ten loses more than 5,800 EUR and the worst lost 15,700. If the robot works for a year and then turns to noise (my diagnostic), P typically loses about 7,400 EUR, against 9,500 for C2 and 13,100 for A.
- **The -50 % stop must be off.** With it left on, P is stopped in 75 % of half-edge paths and its median gain is -675 EUR.
- **No advantage when the rules just cover costs, or in year one.** At edge 0, P's median is -2,766 against -2,344 for A, with 81 % of paths in loss against 56 %; only the tail is shorter. At 12 months and edge -0.5, P loses 2,513 against 2,258 for A.
- **The half-edge price is larger than "17 % against 6 %".** P ends below C2 in 90.6 % of paths. In 10 % of paths it pays 5,000 EUR or less and ends at -2,342 where C2 would have ended at +10,227.
- **The trial budget is spent at 5 % risk.** When the rules are worthless, 96 % of the 3,000 EUR is lost and the account is then too small to trade.

**Two figures to soften.** The quarter-edge "+1,500" ranges from -926 to +1,502 across five draws, so "about zero" is the honest wording. At half edge P is 26,600 to 29,000; P2 equals the flat 1 %, not more.

**Where the protection comes from.** It comes from paying less, not from timing. Paying 3,000 EUR and then nothing gives the same median at edge -0.5 (-2,807, worst -2,977). Paying 31 months regardless gives -16,899. The same amounts paid blind to results do better than P at half edge (median 32,918, 8.2 % in loss). The switch is a slow detector: at month 4 it pays in 56 % of half-edge paths and 20 % of worthless ones; at month 12, 62 % and 4 %.

**Sensitivity and the 1 % trial.** The ranking of P against A and C2 holds for thresholds 0.9 and 1.1, for 2 or 4 trial payments, for blocks of 4 and 13 weeks, and for two other seeds. P run at 1 % loses 1,047 EUR at 12 months in the worthless case instead of 2,513, but about the same at 36 months (2,366), and gains 21,700 instead of 29,000 at half edge.

The corrected sentences are in the findings. Everything is in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-gold-orb/340d9f5a-4d28-5733-90cb-10a10699d00b/scratchpad/growth/adversarial_steps/`.
